title: Is Subsequence
spaceBreakdown:
- int i, j, n, m: four scalars → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion → O(1)
- not counted: input strings s and t
approach: Use two pointers: one index into s and one into t. Scan t left to right; whenever t[j] equals s[i], advance i. If i reaches the end of s, every character of s was matched in order, so s is a subsequence. This is correct because the greedy choice of matching each character of s to the earliest available occurrence in t never hurts later matches - any valid match can always be shifted left.
hints: If you could only read each character of t exactly once, in what order would you need to match the characters of s? s.length ≤ 100 and t.length ≤ 10^4.
Two pointers: one index into s, one into t. Walk t left to right; when t[j] == s[i], advance i. Example: s = "abc", t = "ahbgdc" - at j = 0, t[0] = 'a' matches s[0], so i moves to 1.

**Empty s** - s has zero characters
`Input: s = "", t = "ahbgdc"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning `i > 0` instead of `i == n` → returns false

**s longer than t** - s has more characters than t
`Input: s = "abc", t = "ab"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning `j == m` instead of `i == n` → returns true

**Duplicate characters in s** - s has repeated characters
`Input: s = "aaa", t = "baaab"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: incrementing j only inside the match branch, not on mismatch → infinite loop

**No characters match** - s and t share no common characters
`Input: s = "xyz", t = "abc"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning `true` unconditionally after the while loop exits → returns true

followUps.q: If there are billions of s strings to check against the same t, how would you preprocess t?
followUps.a: Build a map from each lowercase letter to a sorted list of its indices in t. For each s, maintain a current position in t and binary-search the next occurrence of each character of s after that position. TC: O(|t| + k·|s|·log|t|) for k queries, SC: O(|t|) for the index map.

followUps.q: What if t arrives as a streaming input too large to store?
followUps.a: Maintain only the pointer i into s. For each incoming character of t, if it equals s[i], advance i. Return true once i reaches the end of s. TC: O(|t|), SC: O(1). This handles one s at a time and cannot reuse work across multiple s values.

followUps.q: What if both s and t can be up to 10^9 characters?
followUps.a: The two-pointer approach still runs in O(|t|) time, but you must stream both strings in fixed-size chunks instead of loading them into memory. Keep i, j, and the chunk buffers; process one chunk of t at a time. TC: O(|t|), SC: O(chunk size) = O(1) relative to input.
